title: Nicaea (325)
hookLine: bishops gather over Arius' teaching and write: of one substance with the Father

cards: One Greek word: homoousios. Bishops traveled across the empire to argue over it, emperors took sides, and people were sent into exile for saying it or for refusing to. Here's why.

In Alexandria, a priest named Arius was teaching that the Son of God was the first and greatest thing God made. Glorious, above everything else, but made: not God in the same way the Father is God. His bishop objected.
The argument spread, and the emperor Constantine called bishops together at a city called Nicaea to settle it.

teach.h: ARIUS: THERE WAS WHEN HE WAS NOT.
teach.b: Arius wasn't a careless thinker. He was protecting something: God is one, and nothing can share God's being. So the Son, he reasoned, must be something God made.
The creed that came out of Nicaea ended by rejecting a saying of his side, that there was a time when the Son was not.
The bishops, Athanasius later wrote, searched the Bible for words to answer him, and kept finding that Arius could agree with them. The Son is from God? Yes, he'd say, so is everything.
So they reached for a word that isn't in the Bible at all. Homoousios: of the same being, of one substance. The Son isn't like the Father in a high and noble way.
He is what the Father is.

teach.h: A WORD FROM OUTSIDE THE BIBLE.
teach.b: A word from outside scripture, chosen to protect what they believed scripture already said. John's Gospel opens, "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."
And Jesus says in John, "I and my Father are one." The bishops heard those lines as more than closeness. The creed later prayed in churches is a fuller form, which we'll meet later on this path.

teach.h: OF ONE SUBSTANCE WITH THE FATHER.
teach.b: In the old English of the Book of Common Prayer, its lines on the Son run: "Very God of very God, Begotten, not made, Being of one substance with the Father." Very, there, means true.
Begotten, not made: a son, not a product. Why does it matter? Christians who say this creed are saying that when they look at Jesus, they aren't looking at God's best creation.

how: Christians in Orthodox, Catholic, Anglican, Lutheran and other churches say the Nicene Creed together in worship, standing, often on Sundays.

games.q: you're a bishop at Nicaea. every Bible phrase you offer, Arius can agree with. what do you do?
o: keep quoting the Bible until he gives in.
pick one word from outside the Bible that he can't accept.
go home. the question can't be answered.
games.why: they chose homoousios, of one substance, a word Arius couldn't say, to protect what they believed scripture meant.

practice: If the Nicene Creed is part of your tradition, say it slowly now and stop on the lines about the Son. If it isn't, let four phrases go by, one per breath: God of God, light of light, very God of very God, begotten, not made.
Don't try to solve them; just notice which one catches.

wordCard.voice: Homoousios. Greek for of the same being, of one substance. The word the bishops at Nicaea chose to say the Son is what the Father is, not something the Father made.

orig.note: Greek: of the same being, of one substance. the word at the heart of the creed of Nicaea.

carryVoice: Your line: true god from true god. One word, guarding a whole belief. Until tomorrow.
